reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on very easy, consistent runs, it lacks any structured progression or stimulus for speed. Plan B incorporates a longer run (60 minutes) to build endurance, a cross-training session to maintain fitness without excessive impact, and a single longer run to simulate trail conditions. This variety is crucial for developing both aerobic capacity and trail-specific adaptations needed for faster times, whereas Plan A’s repetitive easy runs will likely lead to plateaus.
